_comment: Question bank for bulk AI-answer testing (test_ai_on_bank.py).
Add as many questions as you want -- there's no fixed count like
the 5-question quizzes in test_bot.py.
Each entry:
id       -- stable number/string you'll reference later in
'deep investigate' mode to re-ask just that question.
Keep these stable once assigned -- don't renumber
existing entries, or old miss-reports will point at
the wrong question next time you run bulk mode.
text     -- the question. For bare-letter style (options embedded
in the question, like the real bot's Q1/Q5), write the
'A) ...' / 'B) ...' lines directly into this string,
same as test_bot.py's bare_letters questions do.
options  -- list of option strings. For bare-letter style, this is
just ["A", "B", "C", "D"] (see bare_letters below) --
same convention test_bot.py already uses.
correct  -- 0-based index into options of the right answer.
bare_letters -- true if options are embedded in text (see above),
false if options holds the real option text.
This mirrors test_bot.py's existing question dict shape exactly, so
the same _build_prompt() / _options_are_bare_letters() logic in
run_challenge.py applies unchanged.

questions.text: What is a trader actually paid from, once funded?

Do firms that disclose Demo accounts also tend to convert to live accounts?
A) Yes, always
B) Only sometimes
C) Not addressed
D) No
$50,000 account, 5% daily / 10% total drawdown. Day 3 closing loss for the day is $2,400, from a balance that was already down $2,000 from Day 2. Any limit breached?

$10,000 account, 5% daily drawdown. A trader's loss for the day lands at exactly $500. Has the daily limit been breached?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only combined with total drawdown
D) Not enough information

$20,000 account, 10% total drawdown. Balance falls to exactly $18,000. Evaluation failed?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only if it also happened in one day
D) Depends on the firm

1-step evaluation. Is the total drawdown limit higher or lower than a 2-step's?
A) Higher
B) Lower
C) Identical
D) Not stated

A trader is profitable on 4 separate days but only trades on 2 days total that month. Does this satisfy every version of the Consistency Rule described?
A) Yes, always
B) No, never
C) Only for firms with a minimum-trading-days requirement
D) Only for 1-step evaluations

A trader grows their balance by 0.4% on a given day. Does that count as a "profitable day" under the Consistency Rule?
A) Yes, any growth counts
B) No, growth must be positive but the bar is unspecified
C) Only 0.5% or more counts, per the note
D) Not addressed

A trader passes a $10,000 challenge, gets funded, then later violates the daily drawdown rule while funded. Does the funded account size stay $10,000?
A) Yes, same size as evaluation
B) No, funded accounts are always larger
C) Not addressed
D) Only if they didn't violate any rules

Is twice-a-month payout the industry standard, or one firm's specific policy as described in the note?
A) Industry standard
B) One firm's example
C) Universal minimum
D) Universal maximum

Which profit split is described as the universal rule across all prop firms: 80/20 or 90/10?
A) 80/20
B) 90/10
C) Neither is universal
D) Both, depending on account size

Does the note state that every prop firm gives funded traders a Demo account, or that most do?
A) Every firm, no exceptions
B) Most firms, with rare exceptions
C) Only firms that were sued
D) Split evenly between demo and live

Where does the money for a funded trader's payout literally come from, according to the note?
A) Their own demo trading gains
B) The firm's investment portfolio
C) The pool of evaluation fees paid by all entrants
D) A government-backed guarantee fund

According to the note, what fraction of prop firms eventually convert consistently profitable traders to live accounts?
A) Exactly 10%
B) Roughly half
C) A specific number is not given — only described as rare
D) The majority

Did U.S. and Canadian courts prove that My Forex Funds manipulated prices, or does the note describe this as an allegation?
A) Proven in court
B) Described as an allegation
C) Confirmed by Trustpilot reviewers
D) Neither — only the business-model lie was addressed

Does a high Trustpilot rating, per the note's own point, mean a prop firm is safe from these issues?
A) Yes, that's the note's point
B) No — the note uses My Forex Funds' 4.8 rating to show reputation isn't proof of safety
C) Only if the rating is above 4.5
D) Not addressed at all

After the My Forex Funds incident, does the note say ALL prop firms now disclose Demo accounts, or most?
A) All, without exception
B) Almost every firm
C) Only firms operating in Ethiopia
D) Not addressed

The note states 90%+ of new traders fail. Fail at what, specifically — the funded/live account, or something else?
A) The funded account after passing
B) New traders in trading generally, not the evaluation specifically
C) The consistency rule specifically
D) Not enough information to say

Does the note give a specific number of "hidden rules" firms commonly impose?
A) Yes, typically 3-5
B) No — only describes them as "many," unquantified
C) Yes, exactly one per firm
D) The note says hidden rules are rare, not common

Does the note claim price manipulation is confirmed across the prop firm industry generally, or specific to one firm with a broader suspicion noted separately?
A) Confirmed industry-wide
B) Confirmed only for My Forex Funds, with a separate general "reasonable to suspect" framing
C) Never mentioned outside My Forex Funds
D) Confirmed for all firms that offer Demo accounts

Per the note's recommendation, does picking a regulated, licensed, reputable firm guarantee no price manipulation or improper payout practices?
A) Yes, that's what regulation guarantees
B) The note frames it as a check to make, not a guarantee
C) Only for firms operating in the U.S. or Canada
D) Not addressed

Once a trader is funded, does the Consistency Rule the note describes stop applying, or continue?
A) Stops — it's evaluation-only
B) Continues — funded traders remain under the same rules
C) Only continues for 2-step evaluations
D) Not addressed for funded traders

Does the note quantify how much of total firm revenue comes from evaluation fees versus other sources?
A) Yes, a specific percentage is given
B) No — only that fees are described as the primary revenue source, qualitatively
C) The note says fees account for exactly half
D) The note says fees are a minor, secondary source

For a 2-step evaluation, is the daily drawdown limit ever stated as different from the 5% most-common figure?
A) Yes, 2-step always uses a lower daily limit
B) No differentiation is given for daily drawdown by step count — only total drawdown is said to vary
C) 2-step uses a higher daily limit
D) Not addressed for either
